doc.title: Hank Cicalo interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 30, 2022

title: Most enjoyable artists: Peggy Lee and prepared artists
summary: Hank says the best sessions come when artists arrive prepared, citing Peggy Lee, and contrasts those who work everything out in the studio.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: I see. What are the most memorable artists that you’ve — I know it’s like hundreds and hundreds of people that you’ve recorded, what stands out for you as one of the most enjoyable experiences?

The enjoyable experience is when the artists really come in knowing what they want to do. Like I worked with Peggy Lee — always on time, always ready. Always she had the tune down. You know everything, no problems, we just did it. And there’s those artists

they never went to the meetings with the artist and the producer — I mean the artist and the engineer or the artist and the band. If the artist doesn’t go with those meetings he’s losing something. You want the artist to be there with the producer or if the artist is the producer to work with the arranger. You don’t want them doing that stuff on the date. That kills you. Now there are some producers who like to work that way. Like they want the creativity to be instant. You know like it happened in the studio. Some come in very prepared with an arranger or whatever and work very well. Some come in with nothing and they work it out in the studio. Depends on the artist. I’ve worked on both. I’ve worked when an artist comes in and they want it to be a single and they’re really working on it and a guy comes in and he’s never seen the tune he’s working on it five or six hours. That’s painful.
